properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/02/2024
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8209794
Permit API: 003-22628
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Findlay Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/02/2024
Comments: On December 2, 2024, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a reported release that reportedly occurred on site on December 1, 2024 at 1:15pm. The incident was reported to the Department by Nate Smeill (Range Resources) on December 1, 2024 at 2:29pm as an approximate 10 gallon release of produced water to the gravel well pad. The Department spoke with Smiell via phone call upon arriving to the site at 11:50am. According to Smiell:- the 10 gallon release of produced water was determined to be a visual estimate in terms of amount released- the release occurred when the driver of a water truck hauler failed to close the bleeder valve on the truck when filling the truck with produced water- all impacted material was placed into the roll off box that remains on site at this time- only work left to be done for remediation is new gravel back fill at area of release- a spill report will be sent to the Department later todayThe ESCGP (ESX17-003-0002) was issued on 9/20/2017 and was set to expire on 9/19/2022. The Notice of Termination (NOT) was submitted by the Operator on 11/3/2020 and was approved by the Department on 11/16/2020.Act 9 sign present on site. Access road is in good condition with no erosion and/or sedimentation (ES) issues observed. Emergency Response Plan, Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, and ESCGP plans are all present on site. Area of where the produced water was released is observed in Photos 8-9, the roll off box containing the impacted material is observed in Photo 10, and a measure of specific conductivity within the area of release is observed in Photo 11, showing proper remediation of the area in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1).Violations for the release are being issued and immediately corrected.

Comments: The DEP completed an administrative inspection on Seneca Resource's Peffer-Strong 483 35H 53580 well (117-22110) located in Sullivan Township, Tioga County on 7/7/2022. This inspection was completed in order to summarize sample results from a sample collected during the 6/23/2022 inspection (Inspection record #3381709). On 6/23/2022, the DEP conducted a routine inspection of the Peffer-Strong 483 well site and discovered elevated electrical conductivity fluid on the pad surface (field measured at ~7.35mS/cm). A sample (0983-310) was collected from the fluid and was submitted to the DEP laboratory for standard analysis code 942. Final sample results for 0983-310 were received by the DEP on 7/7/2022. The DEP's analytical sample results are attached as photos and as a file. Additional information regarding the initial inspection on 6/23/2022 and a follow-up inspection on 7/1/2022 can be found in inspection records #3381709 and #3387753. The operator was notified of the findings via phone from the 6/23/2022 inspection report on 6/23/2022. The operator was also notified of the findings via phone from the 7/1/2022 inspection report on 7/1/2022. The operator explained that they were awaiting the DEP's sample results prior to conducting any sort of remedial work onsite.Based on the findings of the inspections conducted on 6/23/2022 and 7/1/2022 and based on the analytical sample results found in this report, violations of the following are cited against API #117-22110 at this time:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 691.402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 11/18/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8256580
Permit API: 083-46720
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/18/2025
Comments: I was informed by my supervisor that Bull Run Resources had reported a release at their Backwards L #3 well located in Hamilton Township, McKean County. A gathering line failed and an unknown amount of crude oil was released. The release traveled down a road ditch approximately 500 feet heading in a southwest direction to a culvert crossing. The release continued through the culvert heading north for close to 190 feet, before stopping in what is best described as an infiltration sump for the ditch line. The sump contained the release and prevented it from reaching Chappel Fork. JR from Bull Run was onsite with a mini excavator and a lined dumpster that was being filling with impacted soil. He is continuing to work his way down the ditch line removing impacted soil and debris. The sump will be cleared of leaves and debris before being pumped out. Impacted soil will be removed and disposed of at an approved facility. Future inspections will be performed to document the ongoing cleanup. Confirmatory sampling of the remediated area is expected to be conducted when remediation is complete. Documentation regarding the disposal of the contaminated soil is also expected to be provided to the Department.Please acknowledge receipt of this inspection and attached violations by emailing me at ebruce@pa.gov.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a Follow-up inspection of the Tilden Marcellus - Thomas 808 well pad located in Elk Twp, Tioga Co. on 7/9/2019 @1015 hours. The weather was 72 degrees and sunny, humidity 73%, no wind. Activity onsite consists of Tilden Marcellus finishing plumbing in the recently completed wells and removing the temporary flow back equipment. Jenn Compton and Taylor Parsons, Tilden Marcellus/Rockdale were present onsite for the inspection. As of today's inspection most of the secondary containment and rig mats have been removed. Tilden Marcellus is currently performing screening and removal of pad material impacted by stimulation activities, and the reported release on 6/3/2019. Ms. Compton stated in addition to the eastern pad edge and fill slope, an area in the center of the pad was found to have material with an elevated conductivity. The removed material was observed stockpiled in secondary containment, and covered in tarps. Trucks were observed removing fluid from the tank farm located along the northern cut slope. Fluid with an elevated conductivity was observed in both layers of secondary containment. A puddle/muddy area against the foam berm (photo#6) had a field measured conductivity of 3.28mS/cm. Mr. Parsons was notified of my findings regarding the tank farm. He stated a site truck was being dispatched to clean out the containments, and additional containment would be constructed in the truck load area to prevent spills to the ground surface from hose breaks. Violations of 25 Pa Code 78a.57a and SWMA 610(2) cited 6/17/2019 in IR#2894467, due to the operation of an illegal waste transfer station, are CORRECTED at this time. Tilden Marcellus ceased hauling and storage of fluids when notified of the violations. A NOV response was received on 7/9/2019. Violations of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301 and 25 Pa Code 78a56(a), cited 6/4/2019 in IR#2889847, remain OUTSTANDING against API#117-20478 from a previous release. Site remediation is ongoing. Once a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEP's Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review, and attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed, the outstanding violations will be closed. No additional violations are cited at this time. Please ensure any deficiencies noted are addressed and contact me with any questions. I departed the site at 1130 hours.

Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's Twin Ridge 02-185 well site located in Covington Township, Tioga County on 1/27/2020 at 1020 hours. The weather was 32 degrees with cloudy skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a reported release to containment on the pad. I spoke with Jeff Sparks (Repsol) onsite. On Saturday 1/25/2020, a hose connection between two frac tanks that were holding collected high pH stormwater from the basins onsite froze up and ruptured. The cold temperatures caused water to freeze and the expansion ruptured the hose connection between the two tanks pictured in photo #6. A reported two-foot level of water drained out of the tanks and into the secondary containment This resulted in an estimation of 100 barrels of released stormwater from the tanks. While onsite today, I observed a large volume of ice and water still present within the secondary containment. I told the operator that the containment should be cleaned out and inspected to ensure its functionality. Most of the fluids surrounding the containment and across the pad were frozen but any liquid water was screened for conductivity and pH. Puddles surrounding the containment were similar to those in other areas of the pad. No evidence was available to show that the secondary containment had leaked any volume of the reported release. The remainder of the site was routinely inspected. Crew were onsite today performing work on some of the processing facilities. All containment structures were intact and no leaks were noted. No erosional issues were found onsite today. Stormwater basins are continuing to be pumped out periodically. Violations cited on 6/24/2019 remain OUTSTANDING against API 117-21997 at this time. The violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has been confirmed. No additional violations were noted today.

Violation ID: 8286874

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 8/28/2026
Comments: On August 28, 2026, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response inspection at the Range Resources Laurel Hill Well Pad B. Range Resources Kirby Steck reported on August 27, 2026 at 2135, a gasket for a filter pod failed causing a release of reuse water outside of containment. The filter pod was associated with a WMGR123 onsite supporting the Bear Hollow Well Pad stimulation. Upon arriving onsite, Range Resources had initially estimated the spill to be 15 to 20 gallons. When the DEP arrived onsite, Range Resources contractor had begun excavating the area of the fill slope of the well pad impacted by the release. The area of excavation at the time of arrival was approximately 10 feet by 10 feet and about 18 inches deep. Soil conductivity of the impacted area ranged from 3,000 to 6,000 uS/cm. Range Resources contractor continued to excavate the area of impact during the inspection. The area of impact had increased to approximately 20 feet by 10 feet and approximately 3 feet in depth. At 3 feet depth, Range Resources was finding elevated soil conductivity levels of 6,000 uS/cm. Prior to the DEP leaving the site, Range Resources determined that they would proceed with remediating the spill through the Act 2 process due to the spill being larger than initially estimated.Violations of Chapter 78a.56(a), Clean Streams Law 402(b), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted due to the release of reuse water outside of secondary containment onto the well pad slope.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on all (6) wells on the Aukema pad. The Aukema 3H, 4H, 7H, 1HC, 2HC and the 101HC wells. These tests are being performed to assess the results of the initial remedial deployment of Renegades localized casing expansion tool in the production casing of the Aukema 1HC and 101HC wells on 5/17/21 and 5/18/21 and the 3H and 2HC between 1/24 - 27/21. This is the second round of testing since initial remedial work was performed. SPBUTs were initiated on 12/6/21 @ ~ 08:45 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (6) wells annuli are shut in. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Trey Sites amd Dalton Johnson and Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andrew Pfisterer. Starting at approx. 09:00, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Some sediment accumulation noted within this area, which appears to be from runoff on the upper portion of this section (Photos 17, 18).The operator has failed to maintain the access road in accordance with 102.22(a) regulations. Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Spring Creek Road in July 2008. A spill was reported to the Department at 16:28 on April 1, 2019. The spill occurred when the brine tank overflowed. Oil was allowed to escape and contact the ground surface, but no evidence of a brine discharge could be seen. The reported release amount was of approximately 30 gallons, and conditions at the site at the time of inspection indicate that this estimate is reasonable. Because the estimated spill volume was less than 1 bbl, a visual clean-up at this site is appropriate. A culvert under the access road has overtopped, allowing sediment to be carried into the stream in this HQ watershed. As per a phone call with Joshua Martz from Diversified at 11:50 on April 2, equipment is expected to arrive on site in the morning of April 3. The visual cleanup of the site is expected to be completed at that time. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil & Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

Comments: This conventional well is equipped to produce with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack. There are no surface concerns evident on the well site at this time. 2025 APR and MIA information were submitted for this well.The tank battery for Trinity Mineral Partners' Roell lease is located approximately 500 feet to the west of this well, and is accessed off of Rounds Hill Road.This tank battery consists of two earthen containments. One containment consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks and separators, there are no surface issues evident at this containment. A second earthen containment (located southwest/downslope of the aforementioned one) holds a horizontal (approximate 250 bbl capacity) steel production water tank. There is an approximate 10' x 200' area that has been recently excavated beyond the end of the spur road that is used to access the tank battery, and continues adjacent to and downslope of, the production water tank/containment and ends at the edge of the bank that runs parallel to Rounds Hill Road. Mulch has been sparsely applied across the excavated area. Deer tracks are prevalent throughout the excavated area downslope of the production water tank/containment.Water is seeping out of the southwest corner of the production water tank containment, the specific conductance (SPC) of this water is elevated (> 1000 uS/cm). The SPC of the material at (and downslope of) the southwest corner of the production water tank containment is also elevated. Elevated SPC continues to be observed in standing water and the soil within the aforementioned excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment. Beyond the excavated area, there is an approximate 50 foot section of stressed vegetation evident on the bank of Rounds Hill Road. The SPC of the soil along this section of road bank is also elevated. The SPC of the Rounds Hill Road ditch water downslope of the aforementioned area of stressed vegetation is approximately ten times higher than the ditch water upslope of this point. The Rounds Hill Road ditch water continues to have elevated SPC for another 200 feet until the ditch enters an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Jackson Run.There was no obvious discharge from the production water tank during this inspection, the prevalence of elevated SPC and stressed vegetation in the material that comprises the containment and areas downslope of the containment is indicative of production water discharges into the containment due to poor housekeeping and/or a lack of tank integrity. The evidence obtained during this inspection also indicates that the containment surrounding the production water tank was not constructed in a manner to prevent the tank contents from reaching waters of this Commonwealth.An SAC 942 water sample was collected from standing water located in the excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment.In addition to the information requested in the attached Notice of Violation, it is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners reveal how the aforementioned excavated soil was disposed and provide any supporting documentation regarding its disposal.

A second earthen containment (located southwest/downslope of the aforementioned one) holds a horizontal (approximate 250 bbl capacity) steel production water tank. There is an approximate 10' x 200' area that has been recently excavated beyond the end of the spur road that is used to access the tank battery, and continues adjacent to and downslope of, the production water tank/containment and ends at the edge of the bank that runs parallel to Rounds Hill Road. Mulch has been sparsely applied across the excavated area. Deer tracks are prevalent throughout the excavated area downslope of the production water tank/containment.Water is seeping out of the southwest corner of the production water tank containment, the specific conductance (SPC) of this water is elevated (> 1000 uS/cm). The SPC of the material at (and downslope of) the southwest corner of the production water tank containment is also elevated. Elevated SPC continues to be observed in standing water and the soil within the aforementioned excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment. Beyond the excavated area, there is an approximate 50 foot section of stressed vegetation evident on the bank of Rounds Hill Road. The SPC of the soil along this section of road bank is also elevated. The SPC of the Rounds Hill Road ditch water downslope of the aforementioned area of stressed vegetation is approximately ten times higher than the ditch water upslope of this point. The Rounds Hill Road ditch water continues to have elevated SPC for another 200 feet until the ditch enters an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Jackson Run.There was no obvious discharge from the production water tank during this inspection, the prevalence of elevated SPC and stressed vegetation in the material that comprises the containment and areas downslope of the containment is indicative of production water discharges into the containment due to poor housekeeping and/or a lack of tank integrity. The evidence obtained during this inspection also indicates that the containment surrounding the production water tank was not constructed in a manner to prevent the tank contents from reaching waters of this Commonwealth.An SAC 942 water sample was collected from standing water located in the excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment.In addition to the information requested in the attached Notice of Violation, it is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners reveal how the aforementioned excavated soil was disposed and provide any supporting documentation regarding its disposal.

Violation ID 769370
Permit API 081-21470
Unconventional Y
County Lycoming
Municipality Eldred Twp
Inspection Type Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date 2016-09-22
Comments Routine Inspection; 9/22/2016. Inflection Energy notified the Department of a release of produced water/blended water to the gravel pad surface. According to the notification, the elevated conductivity was just recently discovered and the release was estimated at 25 gallons but the release was being investigated further. I entered the site off Yeagle Road at 14:28 and met with Inflection Energy representatives. At the time of the inspection CalFrac was completely rigged-down and had left the site. Onsite at the time were the two fresh water tanks, one waste tank, centrifuges, filters, working tanks, sand equipment and containment around the well heads. Personnel onsite were vacuuming water which was accumulated on the gravel pad surface between the working tanks and the sand equipment (north of the well heads). Personnel onsite also excavated pad material on the north and east sides of the working tanks. Water in both of these excavations (on the pad surface) had field conductivity between 800-1,100 umhos/cm. Water accumulated on the pad surface west of the working tanks (between the working tanks and the sand equipment) had field conductivity between 6,300-6,600 umhos/cm. Sample 3440292 was collected from water ponded in this area at 14:45 (photo attached). After collecting the sample noted above, I walked the site with representatives of Inflection Energy. Field conductivity of water on containment on the site was between 1,250-1,400 umhos/cm. The centrifuge was in use at the time and field conductivity of water ponded nearby was 162-170 umhos/cm. Finally, field conductivity in a puddle (on the pad surface) between the main pad containment and the sand equipment was 2,400 umhos/cm. Based on my field investigation, conductivity was highest around the working tanks. I recommend evaluating the containment around the working tanks, characterizing the reported release, and notifying the Department of your intent to remediate in accordance with the spill policy. Violations Noted. Routine Inspection; 9/22/2016.

Comments: Arrived onsite for a follow up to inspection 3866602 from 11/12/24 that was conducted in response to a release of produced fluid.The affected area near the wells was excavated and was left open to remove any additional fluid that may collect and to facilitate possible excavation or screening as part of Act 2 remediation.At the time of this inspection, there was some water in the pit that had a conductivity of 5.64 milliesiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). There were no seeps, puddles, or stressed vegetation observed.There are no new violations noted, however there are outstanding violations against the 23HC well for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, 78a56(a), and OGA3218.2(A) from inspection 3866602 conducted on 11/12/24. Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 24 hr. Pressure Build-Up Tests (PBUTs) being performed on both wells on the DeWolf pad, the Evelyn Wyo. 4H and the Evelyn Wyo. 2H. These are the second PBUTs being performed to access recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool) deployment that was performed on both wells on 12/18/20. (Depths of CET deployments were attached to individual well inspections of 2/4/2021. Insp. ID's 2H - 3143784, 4H - 3143787). Both of the Evelyn wells Surface x Intermediate, (13 3/8 x 9 5/8), the Intermediate x Production, (9 5/8 x 5 1/2) annuli and the (20x13) annulus of the Evelyn 2H were shut in on 9/15/21 @ ~ 10:20. All shut-in pressures were monitored and recorded throughout testing period by CALLCs SCADA system. The Evelyn Wyo. 4H wells Conductor x Surface (20 x 13 3/8) annulus has an open casing top in cellar, the Evelyn Wyo. 2H Conductor by Surface (20 x13 3/8) annulus is capped and set up for venting to atmosphere via a 1" pipe to surface and a Sentry valve. Both wells remained in production through the PBUT period. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Matt Clark and Creston Consultant Reps. Tom Messing and Kevin Leaman. Starting at approx. 10:30 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter (cal. 9/16/21)). Gas detections were then confirmed by The Department, using a MSA ALTAIR 5X gas meter, last calibrated on 8/24 /21. Creston Consultant collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for both of the Evelyn Wyo. wells on this pad: - Evelyn Wyo 4H: - (20x13): open casing top in cellar, no bubbling noted. * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 0.0 psi.; 96% gas; Sample taken @ 10:55. - (9x5): 458 psi.; 82% gas; Sample taken @ 11:00. ** The (9x5) annulus vent was opened on 9/16/21 @ 03:30 and shut in after pressure was bled off @~ 03:35. Sample was taken for this annulus @ 11:00. - Evelyn Wyo. 2H: - (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 6% gas; Sample taken @ 10:35. * ECP set on Surface casing. - (13x9): 29 psi.; 90% gas; Sample taken @ 10:45. - (9x5); 182 psi.; 76% gas; Sample taken @ 10:50. - These annular pressure builds-ups show a decrease in pressure since last PBUTs were performed on 5/27/21. - All annuli were returned to venting by 11:05.

Comments: On 03/21/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Hixenbaugh 1-P060 Well Site following violations issued on 02/14/2024 (Inspection Report 3713663, Enforcement ID 425992). Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, and 91.34(a) were issued to the operator for the Department's discovery of oil/grease on the ground at various locations around the well site. The following was observed during inspection on 03/21/2024:The larger area of oil/grease on the ground next to the compressor was removed and new gravel was added. Gravel moved aside to view soils beneath - the oil/grease was removed, clean soils noted (Photos 1-3). The section of oil/grease along the side of the compressor fence/tarp had been removed, some residuals noted along fence line. New gravel added (Photo 4).A waste barrel was noted on site; it was unclear if there was waste within, however I recomend that any waste be removed from site and a manifest be submitted to the Department as soon as possible. Containment was noted (yellow container) next to compressor; buckets on containment (Photos 1, 2). Per the operator's response, they plan to remove the waste barrel pending contractor availability and weather conditions (dated 03/07/2024).It looked as though oil/grease was cleaned up next to the compressor and the trough. I recommend that any oil/grease on the ground be cleaned up as soon as possible and the levels within the trough are monitored (Photos 5-7).A small section of oil/grease was noted on the ground next to the piping that previously displayed tubing. It looked as though repairs were made and the tubing was removed. I recommend that any remaining oil/grease be removed from the ground (Photos 8, 9).The disturbance next to the earthen berm was addressed. A liner and gravel were added along this path. I recommend precautions are taken so that water does not travel underneath the liner and cause accelerated erosion (Photos 10-12). A wet spot was noted on the gravel, however this spot did not display elevated conductivity readings. A small area below the berm drain appeared wet; this area also did not display elevated conductivity readings (Photos 12, 13).The production tank was replaced and gravel was added within the berm and under the new tank. There was a wet spot noted below the piping on the tank, however no elevated conductivity readings were noted (Photos 14, 15).The oil/grease on the ground around the wellhead was removed. Clean soils were noted below the added gravel. I recommend that the wellhead is monitored to avoid any additional oil/grease from reaching the ground (Photos 16, 17). Additional gravel added around production equipment (Photo 18).A buffalo was noted onsite, however contents unknown. Although not required, I recommend that this is placed on containment to avoid any materials from reaching the ground (Photos 18, 19).The access road was in relatively good condition. Some tire ruts noted. There was a pile of dirt next to the road. I recommend that this is removed to avoid any sediment laden runoff, as there is a culvert outlet leading down slope and is approximately 35 feet downslope of this pile (Photo 22).Minor erosion noted at the beginning of the access road leading off into the vegetation. There is a spring on the bank below this area. I recommend that this area of erosion is addressed to avoid any sediment laden water from reaching the main road (Photos 23-25). The violations issued on 02/14/2024 remain outstanding. No additional violations are being issued at this time.

Report Details

Violation ID: 840894
Permit API: 115-20691
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Franklin Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-01-30
Comments: WQS Gene Rickard and I performed an INCDT inspection of the Mitchell well site regarding a reported release which occurred aroung 0830 on Jan. 30, 2019. The complaint number was 339494. The release was reported to me via Briana Cunningham, WQSS. Other individuals on site were Mike Deming and Mr. Otten of Southwestern Energy Production Co. The weather at the time of inspection was around 15 degrees F and snowing. Wind was gusting. At about 0830 hrs. a tank in the onsite tank battery was being filled from a production fluid tank. The operator allegedly was monitoring the tank level from the hatch nearest the front part of the tank. According to a relayed assessment, the operator thought the tank was positioned not quite level, allowing the fluid level to overflow the back part of the tank, spilling onto the containment area surrounding the battery. The containment was later found to be compromised and allowed water to leave the containment area. SWN notified the Department on 1/30/2019. According to onsite representatives, approximately 5-6 bbls. of produced water were released to containment, then through the compromised liner to the pad surface. Resource Environmental was called in to delineate the impacted area, and has been directing a dewatering action to mitigate the impact until the tank battery can be moved, as the tanks are currently frozen to the ground. The timeframe for moving the tanks to delineate the affected area appears to be over the weekend. While onsite, crews were attempting to locate any tears in containment, which was being hampered by the icy buildup inside the containment. Workers were also mobilizing tankers to dewater the area and tanks in the tank battery in preparation for movement off containment to allow resource to delineate the affected area. The affected area seems to stop about 10' from the berm, according to test pits dug for assessment. The spill will be going to Act 2. SWN Representative Mike Deming said a possible change in protocol from a 6" to a 12" tank freeboard is being considered. Violations are attached.

Comments: On April 17, 2026, the DEP conducted a FUI of Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc's Armstrong 2 gas well following IR4155454 where violations were continued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road. Present during today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.A NOV response has yet to be received from the operator of this gas well following IR3891447 when viols were issued however, the DEP has been in communication with the other operator who utilizes the shared portion of the access road. IR4155472 documents the other operator stating they would visit the site to assess the shared road. Observations collected of the shared access road during IR 4155454 include deep erosion rills with water actively flowing down the access road and an exposed and cracked open culvert pipe. During IR 4155454, the DEP requested the operator(s) provide the DEP with a written timeline of remedial actions to repair the access road. To date, this written timeline this has yet to be received. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the shared portion of the access road (Wildcat Road) to be graded with all erosion rills and the exposed culvert pipe removed. Dirt that appeared to be removed from the road during grading was observed to be piled up along the right side of the shared access road. Clumps of this dirt was also observed in the floodway/streambank of a stream located directly downslope and to the right of the shared access road. The broken culvert pipe was observed to be lying on the ground adjacent to the access road, another piece of culvert piping that the broken piece was connected to was still observed to be in the ground and partially buried. Water was not observed to be actively discharging out of this culvert outlet as it appears the inlet may be blocked and resulting in seepage of water along other portions of the access road downslope. The DEP notes that no E and S controls appeared to be installed anywhere along the shared access road. Violations are being issued at this time for sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) and for failure to install E and S controls during earth disturbance activity.At the time of this inspection, no other active E and S issues were observed along the shared portions of Wildcat Road, however, the shared road was not stabilized with gravel and is exhibiting the potential for other E and S issues to occur.The DEP recommends the Operator remove the sediment from the WOC, stabilize the access road, unblock/replace the culvert pipe and install E and S controls along the access road to prevent any further e and s issues.Upon inspection of the direct portion of the access road, conditions appear to be unchanged, the DEP observed large areas of the access road to be flooded. An exposed pipe was observed alongside the access road, however no methane or other odor was detected, the exposed portion of the pipe did not appear to be compromised.At the time of this inspection, the gas well site was still observed to be overgrown with vegetation. A well tag with all required information posted on it was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted wellhead. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the gas wellhead or other production equipment on site at this time, however, a strong gas odor and hissing sound was observed to be coming from the lower portion of the gas wellhead. OGI assistance is being requested at this time to assess the gas wellhead for a gas release. Refer to IR 4183514 for the continuation of violations for heavily rusted production equipment.While onsite, the DEP called the number on the well tag in an attempt to notify the operator of the new violations, however, the number was not in service. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an inadequately stabilized access road are being continued, and new violations are being issued for sediment entering WOC and failure to implement E and S controls.

Comments: At time of inspection, 34 degs. and cloudy. On site today for a Follow Up Inspection (FUI) to confirm that all the wells on this pad have their (13x9) annuli isolated, open and venting to atmosphere. On site w/ me today is OGI Supervisor Ken Kennedy, BKV¿s VP of Operations Lauren Read, Regulatory Mngr. Heather Moyer, Water Mngr. Joe Sodon and Safety Rep. Dale Bennet. The (9x5) annuli are open and venting and are plumbed to surface w/ 2¿ pipe and are tied into a common 2¿ line venting to the production tanks. There were no pressures read on the analog gauges of any annuli at time of this inspection.

Comments: On February 4, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management's Neilan 1 well located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039, where violations were issued for a release from a broken corroded pipe attached to the top of one of the production tanks on site. At the time of this inspection, the well site was snow covered, therefore, the vegetative cover of the well site, along with erosion and sedimentation issues throughout the well site and along the access road could not be assessed at this time.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead. Attached to this wellhead was a small metal production tanks, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of this production tank either. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed some production equipment and a meter box on site, inside the meter box was production paper dated 10/27/2023. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this meter box or the production equipment attached to it. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. The tank on the left did not have any observable holes or corrosive parts, however, the tank on the right still had several corroded pipes at the base of the tank and a pipe that was completely broken in half due to corrosion at the top of the tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near either production tank at this time. During IR 4106039, the Department collected elevated soil conductivity readings at the base of the production tank with the broken piping. At the time of this inspection, the Department was unable to collect soil conductivity readings due to the ground being frozen. However visually, it did not appear that the release had been remediated yet due vegetation being overgrown around the production tank and release area.During IR 4106039, the Department requested the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of that inspection report. The written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, a plan for remediation of the spill or release, and how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requested the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon its receipt. To date, the Department has yet to receive the aforementioned documents. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from broken and corroded piping off of a production tank on site is remaining outstanding at this time.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Twp, Tioga County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/07/2022 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Twp, Tioga county. 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus.  In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/07/2022
Violation Code: 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
Violation ID: 967846
Permit API: 117-22126
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 9/07/2022
Comments: Weather was cool, cloudy, windy and rainy at time of inspection. Upon entering the OSR office, the company man was not present in the office, resulting in longer inspection time. While speaking with the company man Brian Bowers, i was informed that crews were fracking the 78H well and on stage 25 of 63 stages. At time of inspection, company man had no issues or concerns. As of this inspection date there were three more wells to be fracked on the well pad. Isotopic results of gas samples collected from all 3 annuli on 5/2/2022 confirmed the presence of combustible gas at all 3 annular spaces of this gas well. As a result, this violation was originally cited on 5/26/2022 during an administrative inspection (Inspection Record #3368592). No new violations at time of this inspection. All violations are continued from original violation date.
